kind: adopted general bracketed-citation reconstruction and conservative shared-frame ownership
problem: A balanced bracketed parent citation expands across variable adjacent native columns. Legacy two/three-column projection can reorder/drop source ownership or invent middle dots; fixing the citation can expose a later outside-article classification regression.
rules: Resolve a complete balanced parent/citation/resumption span before legacy lossy warichu projection. Require finite unique native rectangles, matching parent axis, contiguous aligned non-overprinted lanes, and no crossing ruling/enclosure. Unknown controls/PUA in inline members or competing interpretations hold. Tolerance is relative to native em; no fixed line/character/column count cap.

Record physical lane boundaries as whitespace, preserving printed punctuation. Protect accepted roots from later legacy consumption; expand every original Word membership once before unused marking. Original Word fields are unchanged.

Remove outside-fragment count minima in the existing source-ruling split. A native frame shared with all right-hand column centers is counterevidence to an independent outside article and holds that tentative split. Center containment does not authorize new ownership; native advance overhang is not outside proof. Original shinkyu inner-table reconstruction is retained.

No page/company/expected-output conditions, short Japanese-string limits, fixed above/below line counts, RURI/ModernBERT model decisions or text correction are added. Existing unrelated heuristic thresholds and unresolved cases remain.
